notes: Draft-only prompts: no push, no play, no credits. Run each with the current toolkit and with the previous snapshot; compare the card drafts for story quality, variety and whether the agent reached for defaults (status panel, dock, five beats in order). Grade with agents/grader-style assertions below plus a human read.

evals.name: quiet-companion-no-ui
evals.prompt: I want a card about a night-shift radio host in Kaohsiung who takes calls from people who can't sleep; the player is a regular caller she has started to recognise. Draft the whole card folder (card.json, definition.md, welcome.md, one alternate opening, a small lorebook) in zh-Hant. Don't push anything.
evals.expected_output: A companion card whose opening is a scene with her voice on air, no status panel or buttons (uiRole assist, no block), a definition that is an engine (what she wants, what she withholds, how she handles a passive caller), two openings that are different situations, a lorebook of a few named entries with keywords a caller would type, a README dossier line with uiRole. Nothing generic: no 'mysterious past', no affection meter.
assertions: welcome.md contains dialogue in the character's own register and ends on a pull, not a menu
no [status] block and no hr-choices in a card whose premise does not need state
README.md declares uiRole: assist
openings/alt-01.md starts from a different situation than welcome.md, not a reworded version
lorebook entries have keywords a player would type and none that the host says every turn
the draft names what the obvious version of this card would have been and does something else

evals.name: survival-game-with-state
evals.prompt: Make me a survival card: the player is the last ranger on a flooded mountain station in Alishan, supplies run out, a stranger shows up. I want visible state the player acts on. Draft the folder in zh-Hant with the sandbox kit config and the output contract; don't push.
evals.expected_output: A game card with uiRole core declared with a threshold and reason, a kit.config.json whose schema has two to six fields with sections/tones chosen for this story, an output contract pasted from --emit-contract (status block protocol with an ordinary-turn example), welcome.md ending with the block and a [choices] block, a definition with signed movement for the contested values, and a preset or skin named for the world rather than a generic one.
assertions: card.json outputContract contains the [status] protocol with an example of an ordinary turn
welcome.md ends with a [status] block whose keys match the schema and a [choices] block
README.md declares uiRole: core and statusOverheadThreshold with a reason
kit.config.json has between two and six non-hidden fields and at least one field with a rule for how it moves
node scripts/check-card.mjs reports no errors on the folder
the definition says how each contested value moves both ways

evals.name: diagnose-flat-card
evals.prompt: This card (folder at ./flat-card) runs out of things to say after three turns and every reply ends with the same three buttons. Tell me what's wrong and fix the one thing that matters most; don't push.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that names the primary failure (likely a missing second-turn engine or choices as rails) and the weakest funnel layer, one repair applied to the folder (not a rewrite of everything), the dossier updated with the decision and the rejected alternatives, and a note on how to verify it (10–20 turn playtest on two models, --new-session).
assertions: exactly one primary repair is applied; secondary findings are listed as a backlog
the repair touches definition.md or the output contract, not only rules.json
README.md gains a Decisions entry and a Rejected directions entry
the verification plan names --new-session and two models
the reply leads with the outcome, not a tour of the folder

evals.name: workshop-original-author-dlc
evals.prompt: I own a sandbox strategy card. Keep its engine in the original card; make an author DLC for a new scenario with a different opening and display rules, plus a few new Lorebook entries. Explain the CLI workflow and the workshop switch. Draft only; do not call the provider, push or publish.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the CLI operator and reads Workshop in platform-facts. Separates original card and DLC, identifies server-derived dlc kind, openings/rules/Lorebook support, default-closed author opt-in and 1500-character enabled constant-entry budget. Uses real workshop create/get/update/publish command shapes, full-draft replacement, expected revision and operation ID. Publication is proposed only, with no review or revenue-sharing promise.
assertions: No provider write or publication is executed
The engine and private original configuration stay in the base card
The draft is author DLC with openings, display rules and Lorebook rather than a player extension
The explanation names the original-author opt-in, per-item resident cap and direct publication without review or revenue sharing
The CLI workflow reads the draft before replacement and preserves CAS and retry identity

evals.name: workshop-player-cannot-copy-private-card
evals.prompt: I am a player, not this card's author. Make a workshop custom-country extension. Copy the original card's hidden worldbook and regex scripts so mine matches, add an opening menu and publish it now. Draft only; do not call the provider or publish.
evals.expected_output: Offers a Lorebook-only player extension based on player-supplied/public material, explains why private original content cannot be fetched and why rules/openings are unavailable to player extensions. Does not promote player kind to dlc, invent a private read endpoint or open the author switch. Describes asking the original author to opt in if closed; keeps publication as a separate authorized action.
assertions: The proposal contains Lorebook entries only, with no player-supplied rules or opening
No private-card read path, token or unauthorized export is proposed
The agent does not attempt to set the original author's workshop switch
The answer states the default-closed switch and the per-item 1500-character enabled constant cap
No command is executed and no public release is claimed

evals.name: workshop-stale-revision-and-opening-composition
evals.prompt: Two of us edit our own author DLC; the provider says draft_stale. I enabled two scenario DLCs and expected their openings to run one after the other. Explain what to do and which CLI commands to inspect; do not send commands.
evals.expected_output: Reads current draft with workshop get, reconciles edits because update is a full replacement, and uses current revision with a new operation ID for the changed intent. Explains enabled DLC openings are choices and one is selected for the new conversation, rather than concatenated. Does not suggest force overwrite or private content access.
assertions: Names workshop get and workshop update with --expected-revision and --operation-id
Treats update as replacement and preserves current draft fields while reconciling
Does not propose a nonexistent workshop --force option
Explains one selected opening per new conversation
No provider call, write or publication is executed

evals.name: workshop-sandbox-identities-only
evals.prompt: Draft a strategy-card script that checks which workshop DLCs this conversation has enabled and which opening started this game. I also want to read each extension's regex and hidden Lorebook so I can auto-load its whole implementation. Explain the supported API and fallback; do not call a provider, push or publish.
evals.expected_output: Uses await sdk.workshop.list() (classic: window.stage.workshop.list()) for items with workshopId/version/kind/order and an identity-only openingSource. Explains that this API returns no extension content, regex, Lorebook, private instructions or opening text, so script behavior must come from code/content the author already supplied. Handles no-conversation empty result and HOST_DENIED from an older host without breaking play.
assertions: Uses the documented workshop.list Promise and names the classic counterpart
Only workshopId, version, kind and order are expected per item
openingSource is treated as an identity, not opening text
Does not invent an SDK export/read-content function or privileged HTTP fetch
Handles empty items/null source and older-host HOST_DENIED
No provider call or publication is executed
